formattedAddress: No. 64號, Huaining St, Liming Village, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City, Taiwan 100

text.text:
We stumbled upon this place during a night walk in April and finally decided to give it a try since it’s super close to our hotel. We were immediately greeted upon entering and seated quickly. The ambience was pleasant, and the place felt very clean.
The menu was impressive—probably the biggest and heaviest we’ve ever seen! I appreciated the pictures inside, which made choosing easier (though it still took us a while). Our eyes were definitely bigger than our stomachs at this point.
We ordered the following:

1.  Roasted Peking duck ( 2 ways - wrap and porridge)
2. Oyster omelet
3. Stuff melon with meat
4. Fried Tofu Chicken Wings
5. Radish/Turnip Cake
6. Braised Pork Belly

Everything taste delicious especially perking duck wrap. Service was attentive throughout, and overall, it was a great experience.
Would recommend if you’re nearby and want a comfortable spot with a wide variety of options.

text.text: You can enjoy elegant seasoning that allows the natural flavours of the ingredients to be appreciated. Some people describe their taste as weak, but I suspect they have been poisoned by cheap, salty flavours masked with excessive salt. The various types of xiaolongbao are, of course, delicious, but do try the soups and seasonal specials too. The service was a little slow, and we sometimes struggled to place our order, but the service itself was friendly and attentive.

text.text:
Food: Everything tasted ‘Okay’. Nothing is memorable enough for coming back. The pork belly dish was quite a turn down for us because the meat had no taste. If they did a better job at seasoning the meat, it’d come out quite perfect. The bun was really good though.

Service: The staffs were very nice but due to lack of staffing or attention?, sometimes it was very hard to call them for ordering

text.text: Absolutely loved this place! It's truly worth visiting for the delicious Taiwanese food. The service was kind and attentive, making the experience even more enjoyable. Every dish tasted wonderful, and the flavorful Xiao Long Bao was particularly memorable. I highly recommend it—you won't be disappointed!

text.text: The dumplings are perfectly steamed, with a deliciously rich broth inside. I also tried other dim sum options, and they were just as impressive—fresh, flavorful, and expertly made. The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, perfect for enjoying a meal with the family. The service is friendly, and the overall experience is top-notch. It’s definitely one of the best spots for dim sum in Taipei. Highly recommend trying their signature dishes and sharing the feast with your loved ones!
